current_text.html: Notice of appeal may be given the court before its adjournment. Written notice of appeal, with supporting reasons, shall be filed by the appellant with both the clerk of the lower court and the clerk of the higher court, within thirty (30) days of notification of the last court's decision. Notification of the last court's decision shall be deemed to have occurred on the day of mailing (if certified, registered or express mail of a national postal service or any private service where verifying receipt is utilized), the day of hand delivery, or the day of confirmed receipt in the case of e-mail or facsimile. Furthermore, compliance with such requirements shall be deemed to have been fulfilled if a party cannot be located after diligent inquiry or if a party refuses to accept delivery. No attempt should be made to circularize the courts to which appeal is being made by either party before the case is heard.

topics: express vs. implied will of session
metadata.synopsis: A ruling elder appealed convictions for distributing an SJC decision contrary to Session's will and for allegedly false, divisive statements in an email opposing a pastoral-election proposal. The SJC sustained the appeal, reversed Session and Presbytery in whole, rendered not guilty, removed the indefinite suspension, and restored him to office. Session could not bind conscience without scriptural authority, and no express prohibition or proof of falsity existed. Many other specifications were rejected; a concurrence cautioned that such emails are rarely wise.

relationships.title: Crouse v. Northwest Georgia Presbytery

metadata.synopsis: A serving deacon nominated for ruling elder complained that his session removed his nomination before BCO 24-1 instruction or examination. The SJC held the session erred by adding an unwritten pre-examination 'vetting' removal and that Northwest Georgia Presbytery erred in approving it: BCO 24-1's sequence—instruction and examination before the session determines eligibility—is mandatory. The ruling reserved the session's sound discretion and the treatment of frivolous or clearly disqualified nominees. The complaint was sustained and remanded for adjudication consistent with the decision.

relationships.title: Edwards v. North Texas Presbytery

occurrences.excerpt: The SJC finds that the case is administratively out order and that it cannot be put in order as the case was never filed with the presbytery or adjudicated below (BCO 42-4 & 43-2).

metadata.synopsis: The SJC held that Jared Edwards's complaint against North Texas Presbytery was administratively out of order and could not be put in order, because the case had never been filed with the presbytery or adjudicated below (BCO 42-4 & 43-2). No merits were reached. The ruling drew 23 concurrences and no dissent; TE Fowler was disqualified as a member of the presbytery party (OMSJC 2.10(d)(3)(iii)). The decision illustrates the SJC's threshold filing requirement: a complaint that bypassed the lower court cannot proceed.

relationships.title: Aven v. Ohio Valley Presbytery

topics: fundamentals of the system of doctrine
metadata.synopsis: An SJC complaint alleged that Ohio Valley Presbytery failed to comply with the SJC's prior remand in Case 2014-01, which required it to 'hear further' from TE Charles Hickey about his changed view on Larger Catechism 177. The SJC denied the complaint. It held that the prior decision neither sustained nor denied the original complaint and prescribed no particular examination procedure; Hickey's nine pages of additional affirmations, exegesis, and answers constituted hearing further, and he addressed the five identified areas at least in part. A concurrence believed the SJC could also have adjudicated the confessional-difference merits; a dissent would have found noncompliance and reached the merits.

metadata.synopsis: The SJC found TE Arnold Robertstad's complaint against North Texas Presbytery administratively out of order and incapable of being put in order under BCO 43-3. Robertstad initially filed by e-mail—not an allowed filing—and his hard-copy filing arrived after the thirty-day deadline. The SJC reasoned that BCO 42-4/43-3 notification language concerns a lower court notifying parties, not party e-filing, and OMSJC 18.10.b bars e-mail filing. The merits were not reached; a concurrence urged later clarification by amendment, and no further proceedings are indicated.

relationships.title: Blevins v. Westminster

metadata.synopsis: SJC sustained TE Philip Blevins's complaint against Westminster Presbytery, holding the Blevins/Seufert complaint was timely despite the commission's February 3, 2004 untimeliness ruling. The wife's April 2003 letter was essentially a BCO 35-13 request to review new evidence, and the Session's May 2003 denial was a new complaintable decision. The SJC did not decide the wife's divorce grounds or the Session's merits; it remanded for Presbytery to rehear the Session and Warhurst complaints with the Blevins/Seufert merits considered. A concurrence added that no full new trial is required.

metadata.synopsis: The SJC found RE Scott Robar's appeal from Central Carolina Presbytery judicially out of order and dismissed it because he filed his notice of appeal only with Presbytery's stated clerk, not also with the General Assembly's stated clerk as BCO 42-4 requires. No merits review of his conviction occurred. Four commissioners dissented, arguing that the presbytery clerk's admittedly incorrect advice, Robar's reliance, and Presbytery's request to treat the appeal as timely should excuse the filing defect under the Plowman precedent and equity or estoppel principles.
